references.text: Solomon's proverbs offer the same wisdom: 'Do not put yourself forward in the king's presence or stand in the place of the great, for it is better to be told, "Come up here," than to be humbled before a noble.' Jesus' teaching in [ref:Ordsp 25:6-7|Proverbs 25:6-7] is a direct parallel to the parable in Luke 14.
[ref:Ordsp 15:33|Proverbs 15:33] states that 'humility precedes honor,' which is precisely the principle Jesus illustrates in this parable—the one who humbles themselves will be honored.

[ref:Ordsp 18:12|Proverbs 18:12] teaches that 'before destruction a man's heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.' Jesus confirms this principle by instructing his listeners to take the lowest place.

The following verse [ref:Luk 14:11|Luke 14:11] summarizes the general principle behind this parable: 'For everyone who exalts themselves will be humbled, and the one who humbles themselves will be exalted.'
In the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector, Jesus repeats the same principle: The one who humbles themselves will be exalted ([ref:Luk 18:14|Luke 18:14]).
Jesus states the same principle in [ref:Matt 23:12|Matthew 23:12]: 'The one who exalts themselves will be humbled, and the one who humbles themselves will be exalted.'
James quotes from Proverbs and confirms: 'God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble' ([ref:Jak 4:6|James 4:6]). Taking the lowest place is an expression of humility that God rewards.
[ref:Jak 4:10|James 4:10]: 'Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.' This is the same principle Jesus illustrates with the parable of the wedding feast.

Peter exhorts: 'Clothe yourselves all with humility toward one another, for God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God so that at the proper time he may exalt you' ([ref:1 Pet 5:5-6|1 Peter 5:5-6]).
[ref:Ordsp 29:23|Proverbs 29:23] declares: 'A man's pride will bring him low, but the humble in spirit will retain honor'—the core message of Jesus' parable.
